title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). There is an extension 1 → π → E → G → 1 and an element ρ of order n in E acting on π by conjugation. Fixing ρ, one wants the solutions g ∈ π of the 'cocycle' equation g ρ(g) … ρ^{n-1}(g) = 1. Equivalently, these are the g such that gρ is again of order n, i.e. the lifts of ρ of order n in π·ρ. This is the non-abelian H^1(Z/n, π) picture.

The tautological representation is g = α ρ(α)^{-1}, with α taken in E_ρ (the elements of E whose image in G commutes with the image ρ̇ of ρ). The set of α giving a fixed g is a right coset of the centraliser E^ρ = Centr_E(ρ). E^ρ always contains ⟨ρ⟩, so α is never unique in E itself. The remedy is condition (29), E^ρ ∩ π = 1, so that E^ρ injects into G^ρ. Then the α giving a solution of (26) correspond to their images α̇ ∈ G, i.e. to the transporter in G of the base class [1]_ρ to the class [g]_ρ. Choosing an element of that transporter chooses α.

Special case on this page:
- π = π_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3}), the free group on two generators, where U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}.
- E = 𝔖_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3}, T_{0,3}), the orbifold fundamental group of U_{0,3} modulo its full automorphism group.
- G = T_{0,3} ≅ 𝔖_3 × Z/2 (permutations of the three punctures, plus complex conjugation).
- ρ is the order-3 lift of z ↦ 1/(1−z).

The conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts of ρ̇ (classes of solutions) are identified with the fixed points U_{0,3}^{ρ̇}. These are the two 'poles' −j and −j̄, the roots of z² − z + 1, i.e. primitive 6th roots of unity. The base one gives the trivial class.

G^ρ = Z/3 × Z/2. Here ρ fixes each pole, while the Z/2 generated by complex conjugation (image of τ) swaps them simply transitively.

Next define E' = π·{1, τ_∞}, the preimage of {1, τ_∞} in E. This is the 'non-oriented triangulated cartographic group' ⟨τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞ | τ_i² = 1⟩ ≅ Z/2 * Z/2 * Z/2, the orbifold group of the closed upper half-plane triangle with reflections. Then:
- (31) E'^ρ = {1}, because E^ρ = ⟨ρ⟩ (the stabiliser of the base pole) and ρ ∉ E'.
- Hence the solutions in π_{0,3} of (32), g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = 1, are in bijection with E' via α ↦ α ρ(α)^{-1}.
- α ∈ π gives the trivial class. α ∈ πτ_∞ gives the other class; the next page computes τ_∞ ρ(τ_∞) = l_1^{-1}.

The next page asks for the profinite analogue. This needs (π̂'·{1,τ_∞})^ρ = 1 and the fact that finite-order elements of 𝔖̂_{0,3} are conjugate to finite-order elements of 𝔖_{0,3}. He then treats the order-2 equation h σ_∞(h) = 1, all of whose solutions are uniquely of the form β σ_∞(β)^{-1}.

Purpose: parametrise solutions of the 3-cycle ('hexagon-type') relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group / équation des lacets by torsion in the orbifold fundamental group of M_{0,4}/symmetries. Note that 𝔖_{0,3} is essentially the extended modular group PGL_2(Z), with π ≅ Γ(2)/±1.
errors: No genuine mathematical error found. All the following check out: G^ρ ≅ Z/3×Z/2, U^{ρ̇} = {−j, −j̄}, the claim that complex conjugation swaps the poles, and (31) given E^ρ = ⟨ρ⟩.
Minor slip in the reference numbering: 'solutions de (28)' should refer to the cocycle equation (26)/(32). (28) is the centraliser definition.
The conventions blur ρ (the element of E) and ρ̇ (its image in G). Also 'τ' and 'τ_∞' are used interchangeably for the lift of complex conjugation.

ideas.what: Solutions of g ρ(g)…ρ^{n-1}(g) = 1 viewed as order-n lifts of ρ, i.e. non-abelian H^1(Z/n, π), parametrised as αρ(α)^{-1} modulo the centraliser of ρ
ideas.modern_name: non-abelian group cohomology / conjugacy classes of torsion sections

ideas.what: Conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts in the orbifold fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞} mod automorphisms correspond to fixed points (−j, −j̄) of the order-3 automorphism
ideas.modern_name: torsion in orbifold fundamental groups ↔ orbifold points (stabilisers); PGL_2(Z) torsion classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (modular group); used in GT theory by Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the modular-type groups and the cartographic groups but not this computation

ideas.what: Explicit bijection: solutions in F_2 of g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = 1 ↔ elements of the non-oriented cartographic group Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 = π·{1,τ_∞}, via α ↦ αρ(α)^{-1}, with the τ_∞-coset giving the non-trivial class
ideas.modern_name: parametrisation of solutions of the GT 3-cycle relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogous lemmas (for f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 and the 3-cycle relation) appear in Drinfeld 1990, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps 1997

ideas.what: Profinite version, requiring that finite-order elements of the profinite completion of 𝔖_{0,3} be conjugate to those of the discrete group, plus vanishing of the centraliser
ideas.modern_name: conjugacy of torsion in profinite completions of virtually free groups / free products (Herfort–Ribes type results)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Herfort–Ribes; used in GT context by Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura

missed.claim: Grothendieck interprets the GT-type 3-cycle relation in F_2 as classifying torsion lifts in the extended modular orbifold group. He uses the reflection (non-oriented cartographic) group Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 as an exact parameter space, with the two classes corresponding to the two elliptic points −j, −j̄ swapped by complex conjugation. The literature has similar lemmas, but the explicit bijection with the non-oriented cartographic group, including the twisted class via τ_∞, is not clearly stated anywhere I know.
missed.quote: l'ens des solutions dans π_{0,3} de l'équation (32) g ρ(g) ρ²(g)=1 est en corr. 1-1 avec l'ens des éléments de π̃_{0,3}=E'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a geometric (orbifold/real-structure) parametrisation of the solutions of the hexagon relation, including a 'non-trivial' class. This is relevant to GT and to real/anti-holomorphic versions of GT.

missed.claim: The profinite statement is left 'à vérifier ultérieurement'. It needs (33) (trivial centraliser in the profinite completion) and conjugacy of torsion in the profinite completion of 𝔖_{0,3}.
missed.quote: si on admet (chose à vérifier ultérieurement) (33) (π̃̂_{0,3})^ρ={1} et que les éléments d'ordre fini de Ŝ_{0,3} sont conjugués des éléments d'ordre fini de S_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This was later settled by general results on profinite free products (Herfort–Ribes), so it is not new. It only shows Grothendieck isolating the right lemma.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, correct orbifold-theoretic treatment of the 3-cycle relation, in line with later GT literature (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps). The explicit use of the non-oriented cartographic group and of the second class via complex conjugation is a nice unpublished detail, but the underlying method is standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'des α avec leurs images α̇ dans G' (correspondence of α with their images), rather than 'des bimorphismes'.
'transporteur de {1}_j dans {g}_ρ' should read 'transporteur de [1]_ρ dans [g]_ρ'.
'i.e. de solutions de (28)' is probably '(26)' in Grothendieck's own numbering slip; the image does read '(26)'-like.
(30) annotation: 'π̃_{0,3} =' (tilde), i.e. E' = π̃_{0,3} = π·{1,τ_∞}; the marginal note reads '(groupe cartographique triangulé pondéré non orienté…)'.
Crossed-out line: 'G^ρ ≃ Z/2Z × {1,τ} ≃ Z… et le groupe…' (deleted).
